head.t: 14 urgent care schemes to receive share of £140m to help tackle winter pressures
head.x: £140 million in funding will be invested in 14 new urgent care schemes across England to help tackle winter pressures, the government has announced, aiming to increase capacity and improve patient flow. These schemes include ED improvements, new urgent treatment centres, and enhancements to digital systems.

head.t: Impact of side hole design of drainage cannulas on flow in veno-venous ECMO circuits – Full Text
head.x: "When reducing the blood-flow rate in ECMO therapy, stagnation areas may develop within the drainage cannula. The geometry of the side holes has an important impact. A comparison of the different designs shows that distal growth of the side hole area results in improved flow behaviour" Bongert et al (2026).

head.t: Non-invasive FFR tool gains US FDA clearance
head.x: Elucid has announced US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) 510(k) clearance of FFR-IQ, its software for non-invasive estimation of fractional flow reserve (FFR) from coronary CT angiography (FFR-CT).

f.t: Apheresis novel double-draw vascular access technique
f.x: "When conservative measures failed, we implemented a novel double-draw technique in which a second draw line was connected via a four-way stopcock and male-to-male adapter to the initial draw access (either a PIVC or port) to improve inlet flow" Sanchez et al (2026).

f.t: Real-time flow monitoring in neonatal infusions
f.x: "We review the mechanisms contributing to flow variability, discuss why conventional pumps cannot verify patient-end drug delivery, and propose a phased pathway for evaluating emerging flow-monitoring technologies" van Rens et al (2026).

f.t: ResMed wins £9.8m, 5-year framework deal to supply Leeds Teaching Hospitals' non-invasive respiratory equipment
f.x: Leeds Teaching Hospitals NHS Trust has awarded ResMed a single-supplier contract worth £9,798,912 (inc. VAT) to supply non-invasive ventilation and high-flow therapy devices, consumables and associated services for five years.
